hook.convey: same whole in equal parts → every part the same size → adding or taking away = counting parts; the part's name (denominator) never changes; a cake in equal pieces, a drawing sheet in equal boxes

use.hi: Ek cake 8 barabar tukdon mein bata hai. Do log usme se tukde lete hain, toh har tukda ek hi size ka hai, isliye bas tukde ginne se pata chal jaata hai ki kitna cake gaya.
use.en: A cake is shared into 8 equal pieces. Two people take pieces from it, and every piece is the same size, so just counting the pieces tells how much cake has gone.

use.hi: Drawing sheet ko 10 barabar khaanon mein baanto aur kuch khaane colour karo. Har khaana sheet ka 1/10 hai, chahe jitne bhi khaane colour karo.
use.en: Split a drawing sheet into 10 equal boxes and colour some of them. Each box is 1/10 of the sheet, however many boxes you colour.

explain.convey: bar in 8 equal parts, 3 shaded = 3/8; each part 1/8, all the same size → adding eighths = counting eighths, the denominator stays 8; the child shades 4 more and names the total (not 7/16)

point.hi: Is bar ke 8 barabar hisse hain aur 3 hisse rangin hain, yaani 3/8. Har hissa 1/8 hai, aur sab hisse ek hi size ke hain. Jab hisse ek size ke hon, toh jodne ka matlab hai hisse ginna, aur hisse ka naam, yaani denominator, wahi rehta hai.
point.en: This bar has 8 equal parts and 3 parts are coloured, that is 3/8. Each part is 1/8, and all the parts are the same size. When the parts are the same size, adding means counting parts, and the name of the part, the denominator, stays the same.

prompt.hi: Is bar ke 4 aur hisse bhi rang do, yaani 3/8 mein 4/8 jodo. Ab bar ka kitna hissa rangin hai?
prompt.en: Colour 4 more parts of this bar, that is, add 4/8 to 3/8. How much of the bar is coloured now?

why.hi: 3 hisse aur 4 hisse milkar 7 aathve hisse, yaani 7/8 rangin hote hain
why.en: 3 parts and 4 parts make 7 eighths, that is 7/8, coloured

simpler.hi: Bar ke 8 barabar hisse hain, 3 rangin: 3/8. Hisse ek size ke hon toh jodna matlab bas hisse ginna, neeche ka 8 wahi rehta hai.
simpler.en: The bar has 8 equal parts with 3 coloured: 3/8. When parts are the same size, adding is just counting parts, and the bottom 8 stays.

explain.convey: taking away on a 0-1 line in tenths: 7/10 is the 7th mark after 0; taking away 3/10 = going back 3 gaps; the gap size does not change, so the denominator stays 10; the child takes 6/10 from 8/10

point.hi: Is line par 0 se 1 tak 10 barabar gap hain, har gap 1/10. 7/10 ka nishaan 0 ke baad saatvaan nishaan hai. Isme se 3 gap peeche aao, toh tumne teen dasve hisse ghataye. Gap ka size nahi badla, isliye denominator wahi rehta hai, 10.
point.en: On this line there are 10 equal gaps from 0 to 1, each gap 1/10. The 7/10 mark is the 7th mark after 0. Go back 3 gaps from it, and you have taken away three tenths. The size of a gap did not change, so the denominator stays the same, 10.

prompt.hi: Isi line par 8/10 mein se 6/10 ghatao. Kitna bacha?
prompt.en: On this same line, take 6/10 away from 8/10. How much is left?

why.hi: 8 gap mein se 6 gap peeche aao toh 2 gap bachte hain, har gap 1/10, yaani 2/10
why.en: go back 6 gaps from 8 gaps and 2 gaps are left, each gap 1/10, so 2/10

simpler.hi: Line 10 gap mein hai, har gap 1/10. 7/10 se 3 gap peeche jao toh teen dasve hisse ghat gaye, aur neeche 10 wahi rehta hai.
simpler.en: The line has 10 gaps, each 1/10. Go back 3 gaps from 7/10 and three tenths are taken away, while the bottom 10 stays.

problem.hi: Gopal ne ek deewar ka 2/11 hissa subah paint kiya aur usi deewar ka 5/11 hissa dopahar mein. Deewar ka kitna hissa paint hua, aur kitna abhi bacha hai?
problem.en: Gopal painted 2/11 of a wall in the morning and 5/11 of the same wall in the afternoon. How much of the wall is painted, and how much is still left?

simpler.hi: Gopal ne deewar ka 2/11 hissa subah aur 5/11 hissa dopahar mein paint kiya. Paint hua hissa aur bacha hua hissa chahiye.
simpler.en: Gopal painted 2/11 of a wall in the morning and 5/11 in the afternoon. We need the part painted and the part left.

givens.hi: deewar 11 barabar hisson mein bati hai
givens.en: the wall is in 11 equal parts

givens.hi: subah 2/11 aur dopahar mein 5/11 paint hua
givens.en: 2/11 was painted in the morning and 5/11 in the afternoon

find.hi: paint hua hissa aur bacha hua hissa
find.en: the part painted and the part left

do.hi: Subah aur dopahar ka kaam jodo
do.en: Add the morning's and the afternoon's work

why.hi: dono gyarahve hisse hain, ek hi size ke, toh sirf upar ke number jodte hain
why.en: both are elevenths, the same size, so only the top numbers are added

simpler.hi: Subah aur dopahar dono gyarahve hisse hain. Isliye bas upar ke numbers jodo: 2/11 + 5/11 = 7/11.
simpler.en: Morning and afternoon are both elevenths. So just add the top numbers: 2/11 + 5/11 = 7/11.

do.hi: Poori deewar ko gyarahve hisson mein likho
do.en: Write the whole wall in elevenths

why.hi: poori deewar mein saare 11 barabar hisse aate hain
why.en: the whole wall has all 11 equal parts in it

simpler.hi: Poori deewar mein saare 11 barabar hisse hain. Isliye poori deewar = 11/11.
simpler.en: The whole wall has all 11 equal parts. So the whole wall = 11/11.

prompt.hi: Poori deewar 11/11 hai aur 7/11 paint ho chuki hai. Deewar ka kitna hissa bacha hai?
prompt.en: The whole wall is 11/11 and 7/11 is already painted. How much of the wall is left?

simpler.hi: 11/11 mein se 7/11 ghatao. Neeche 11 wahi rakho, bas upar ke numbers ghatao.
simpler.en: Take 7/11 from 11/11. Keep the bottom 11 and just subtract the top numbers.

why.hi: 11/11 mein se 7/11 rang hua, toh 11 − 7 = 4 hisse bache, yaani 4/11
why.en: 7 of the 11 parts are painted, so 11 − 7 = 4 parts are left, that is 4/11

answer.hi: deewar ka 7/11 hissa paint hua aur 4/11 hissa bacha hai
answer.en: 7/11 of the wall is painted and 4/11 is left

why.hi: hisse ek hi size ke hain, isliye sirf hisson ki ginti jodi aur ghatayi, aur denominator 11 wahi raha
why.en: the parts are the same size, so only the count of parts was added and taken away, and the denominator stayed 11

prompt.hi: Salma ne ek bottle ka 2/9 juice piya aur Deepak ne usi bottle ka 6/9. Dono ne milkar bottle ka kitna hissa piya?
prompt.en: Salma drank 2/9 of a bottle of juice and Deepak drank 6/9 of the same bottle. How much of the bottle did they drink together?

why.hi: 2 naven hisse aur 6 naven hisse milkar 8 naven hisse, yaani 8/9 hote hain
why.en: 2 ninths and 6 ninths make 8 ninths, that is 8/9

simpler.hi: 2/9 aur 6/9 dono naven hisse hain. Naven hisse naven hi rehte hain, bas unhe gino.
simpler.en: 2/9 and 6/9 are both ninths. Ninths stay ninths; just count them.

prompt.hi: Ek kyari ke 1/8 hisse mein gende lage hain, 2/8 mein gulab aur 3/8 mein tulsi. Kyari ka kitna hissa bhar gaya?
prompt.en: In a flower bed, marigolds fill 1/8, roses 2/8 and tulsi 3/8. How much of the bed is filled?

why.hi: 1 + 2 + 3 = 6 aathve hisse, yaani 6/8, aur hisse ka size wahi hai
why.en: 1 + 2 + 3 = 6 eighths, that is 6/8, and the part size stays the same

simpler.hi: 1/8, 2/8 aur 3/8 sab aathve hisse hain. Neeche wahi rakho aur upar ke teeno numbers jodo.
simpler.en: 1/8, 2/8 and 3/8 are all eighths. Keep the bottom the same and add the three top numbers.

ladder.why: plainest same-denominator sum: sevenths, count the parts
same denominator in a situation: two amounts of phone data in tenths of a GB
two steps in fifteenths: take away a trip, add back a refund, then simplify

remediation.move: same bar, shading grows: 1/5 then 2/5 more → 3 parts shaded, each part still a fifth → the part size never doubles, so the denominator stays 5

say.hi: Ek size ke hisse jodne ka matlab sirf hisse ginna hai. Hisse ka size nahi badalta, isliye neeche ka number wahi rehta hai. Neeche ka number badha diya, toh har hissa chhota ho jaata hai, aur jawab galat ho jaata hai.
say.en: Adding same-size parts just counts the parts. The size of a part does not change, so the bottom number stays the same. If you make the bottom number bigger, every part gets smaller, and the answer goes wrong.

simpler.hi: Hisse ka size wahi rehta hai. Bas upar ke number jodo.
simpler.en: The part size stays the same. Just add the top numbers.

prompt.hi: Jug mein 2/5 litre doodh tha aur 2/5 litre aur daala. Ab jug mein kitna doodh hai?
prompt.en: A jug had 2/5 litre of milk and 2/5 litre more was poured in. How much milk is in the jug now?

why.hi: 2 paanchve hisse aur 2 paanchve hisse milkar 4 paanchve, yaani 4/5 litre hote hain
why.en: 2 fifths and 2 fifths make 4 fifths, that is 4/5 litre

simpler.hi: Dono baar paanchve hisse daale gaye. Paanchve hisse gino; hisse ka naam nahi badalta.
simpler.en: Both times fifths were poured in. Count the fifths; the name of the part does not change.

bridgeToNext.hi: Ab tak saare hisse ek hi size ke the. Agle hisse mein hisse alag size ke honge, jaise chauthai aur aathve hisse, aur pehle unhe ek size ka banayenge.
bridgeToNext.en: So far all the parts were the same size. In the next part the parts will be different sizes, like quarters and eighths, and we will make them the same size first.

simpler.hi: Ab alag size ke hisson, jaise chauthai aur aathve hisson, ko ek size ka banana seekhenge. Board par ek line upar chauthai mein aur neeche aathve mein bati hai.
simpler.en: Now we learn to make parts of different sizes, like quarters and eighths, the same size. On the board one line is split into quarters above and eighths below.

hook.convey: parts of different sizes cannot be counted together → first change both into the same-size parts (common denominator), changing top and bottom by the same factor, then add or take away; half a cup and a quarter cup in a recipe, part of a game level

use.hi: Recipe mein teen-chauthai cup doodh aur ek-tihai cup paani daalna hai. Chauthai aur tihai alag size ke hisse hain, isliye kul kitna hua, yeh jaanne ke liye dono ko ek jaise hisson mein badalna padta hai.
use.en: A recipe needs three quarters of a cup of milk and a third of a cup of water. A quarter and a third are different-size parts, so to know the total, both have to be changed into the same kind of parts.

use.hi: Game ka ek level kal thoda aur aaj thoda khela. Kal tihai hissa poora hua aur aaj aadha, toh dono ko ek jaise hisson mein likhkar hi pata chalega ki level ka kitna hissa ho gaya.
use.en: You played some of a game level yesterday and some today. Yesterday a third got done and today a half, so only by writing both in the same kind of parts will you know how much of the level is done.

explain.convey: one 0-1 line, quarters above, eighths below: the 1/4 mark sits on the 2/8 mark → 1/4 = 2/8; each quarter = 2 eighths, so the top changes by the same factor as the bottom; the child renames 3/4 in eighths (not 3/8)

mustSay.en: both the top and the bottom

point.hi: Is line par upar 0 se 1 tak 4 barabar hisse hain, aur neeche 8. Dekho, 1/4 ka nishaan aur 2/8 ka nishaan ek hi jagah par hain, yaani 1/4 = 2/8. Neeche ka 4 do guna hokar 8 bana, toh upar ka 1 bhi do guna hua. Upar aur neeche dono ko ek hi number se guna karte hain.
point.en: On this line there are 4 equal parts from 0 to 1 above, and 8 below. Look, the 1/4 mark and the 2/8 mark are at the same place, that is, 1/4 = 2/8. The bottom 4 doubled to become 8, so the top 1 doubled too. Both the top and the bottom are multiplied by the same number.

prompt.hi: Isi line par 3/4 kitne aathve hisson ke barabar hai? Jawab aathve hisson wali bhinn mein do.
prompt.en: On this same line, 3/4 equals how many eighths? Give the answer as a fraction in eighths.

ask.hi: 3/4 kitne aathve hisson ke barabar hai?

why.hi: 1/4 = 2/8, toh 3/4 = 3 × 2 = 6 aathve hisse, yaani 6/8
why.en: 1/4 = 2/8, so 3/4 = 3 × 2 = 6 eighths, that is 6/8

simpler.hi: Upar 4 hisse hain, neeche 8, aur 1/4 aur 2/8 ek hi jagah hain. Neeche 4 ka dugna 8 hua, toh upar 1 bhi dugna hota hai.
simpler.en: Above are 4 parts, below 8, and 1/4 and 2/8 sit at one place. The bottom 4 doubled to 8, so the top 1 doubles too.

explain.convey: 1/2 + 1/3: a half and a third are different sizes → on a line in sixths 1/2 = 3/6 and 1/3 = 2/6 → 3/6 + 2/6 = 5/6, never 2/5; the child adds 1/2 + 1/6 on the same line

point.hi: Ab 1/2 + 1/3 jodna hai. Aadha aur tihai alag size ke hisse hain, isliye seedha nahi jud sakte. Is line par 0 se 1 tak 6 barabar gap hain: 1/2 yahan 3/6 par hai aur 1/3, 2/6 par. Ab dono chhathe hisse hain, toh 3/6 + 2/6 = 5/6. Neeche ke number kabhi nahi jodte.
point.en: Now we add 1/2 + 1/3. A half and a third are different-size parts, so they cannot be added straight away. On this line there are 6 equal gaps from 0 to 1: 1/2 is at 3/6 here and 1/3 at 2/6. Now both are sixths, so 3/6 + 2/6 = 5/6. The bottom numbers are never added.

prompt.hi: Isi line par 1/2 + 1/6 kitna hai?
prompt.en: On this same line, what is 1/2 + 1/6?

simpler.hi: Aadhe aur tihaai ka size alag hai, toh pehle dono ko ek size mein badalna hai. Line ke 6 gap mein 1/2 = 3/6 aur 1/3 = 2/6, ab dono jud jaate hain.
simpler.en: A half and a third are not the same size, so first both go into one size. On 6 gaps, 1/2 = 3/6 and 1/3 = 2/6, and now they add.

explain.convey: no line at hand → find the common denominator from the tables: 5 and 4 both reach 20 → 2/5 = 8/20 (× 4 top and bottom), 1/4 = 5/20 (× 5) → 8/20 + 5/20 = 13/20; the child does 3/5 − 1/4 the same way (not 2/20)

point.hi: Jab line na ho, tab tables se samaan har dhoondho. 2/5 + 1/4 mein 5 aur 4 dono ki table mein 20 aata hai. 2/5 ke upar aur neeche ko 4 se guna karo, toh 2/5 = 8/20. 1/4 ke upar aur neeche ko 5 se guna karo, toh 1/4 = 5/20. Ab 8/20 + 5/20 = 13/20.
point.en: When there is no line, find the common denominator from the tables. In 2/5 + 1/4, 20 comes in the tables of both 5 and 4. Multiply the top and bottom of 2/5 by 4, and 2/5 = 8/20. Multiply the top and bottom of 1/4 by 5, and 1/4 = 5/20. Now 8/20 + 5/20 = 13/20.

prompt.hi: Isi tarah 3/5 − 1/4 kitna hai?
prompt.en: In the same way, what is 3/5 − 1/4?

simpler.hi: 5 aur 4 dono ke pahade mein 20 aata hai. 2/5 = 8/20 aur 1/4 = 5/20 banao, phir upar ke numbers jodo.
simpler.en: 20 is in both the 5 and 4 times tables. Make 2/5 = 8/20 and 1/4 = 5/20, then add the top numbers.

problem.hi: Kheer mein 3/4 cup doodh aur 1/6 cup malai daali gayi. Kheer mein kul kitne cup doodh aur malai hai?
problem.en: 3/4 cup of milk and 1/6 cup of cream went into the kheer. How many cups of milk and cream are in the kheer altogether?

simpler.hi: Doodh 3/4 cup hai aur malai 1/6 cup. Dono ko milakar kul cup batane hain.
simpler.en: The milk is 3/4 cup and the cream 1/6 cup. We have to say the total cups of both together.

find.en: 3/4 + 1/6, that is, how many cups in all

do.hi: 4 aur 6 dono ki table mein aane wala sabse chhota number dhoondho
do.en: Find the smallest number in the tables of both 4 and 6

simpler.hi: 4 ke pahade aur 6 ke pahade mein sabse chhota common number dhoondo. Woh 12 hai.
simpler.en: Find the smallest number in both the 4 and 6 times tables. It is 12.

do.hi: 3/4 ke upar aur neeche dono ko 3 se guna karo
do.en: Multiply both the top and the bottom of 3/4 by 3

why.hi: neeche 3 guna hua toh upar bhi 3 guna hona chahiye, tabhi bhinn ki value wahi rehti hai
why.en: the bottom was multiplied by 3, so the top must be too; only then does the fraction keep its value

simpler.hi: 3/4 ke neeche wale number ko 3 se guna kiya, toh upar wale ko bhi 3 se guna karna padega. Isliye 3/4 = 9/12.
simpler.en: The bottom number of 3/4 was multiplied by 3, so the top must be multiplied by 3 too. So 3/4 = 9/12.

do.hi: 1/6 ke upar aur neeche dono ko 2 se guna karo
do.en: Multiply both the top and the bottom of 1/6 by 2

why.hi: 6 ko 12 banane ke liye 2 se guna karna padta hai
why.en: 6 has to be multiplied by 2 to make 12

simpler.hi: 1/6 ke neeche wale number ko 2 se guna kiya, toh upar wale ko bhi 2 se guna karo. Isliye 1/6 = 2/12.
simpler.en: The bottom number of 1/6 was multiplied by 2, so multiply the top by 2 too. So 1/6 = 2/12.

prompt.hi: Ab dono barahve hisse hain. 9/12 aur 2/12 jodo. Kitna hua?
prompt.en: Now both are twelfths. Add 9/12 and 2/12. How much is it?

simpler.hi: 9/12 aur 2/12 ab ek hi size ke hisse hain. Barahve hisse gino, 12 neeche hi rahega.
simpler.en: 9/12 and 2/12 are now parts of one size. Count the twelfths; 12 stays at the bottom.

answer.hi: kheer mein kul 11/12 cup doodh aur malai hai
answer.en: there is 11/12 cup of milk and cream in the kheer altogether

why.hi: dono ko barahve hisson mein badal kar joda, aur 11/12, 3/4 se zyada aur 1 se kam hai, jo theek hai
why.en: both were changed into twelfths before adding, and 11/12 is more than 3/4 and less than 1, which makes sense

prompt.hi: Ek jug mein 2/5 litre paani hai. Usme 1/3 litre paani aur daala. Ab jug mein kitna paani hai?
prompt.en: A jug has 2/5 litre of water. 1/3 litre more water is poured in. How much water is in the jug now?

simpler.hi: 2/5 aur 1/3 ke neeche wale numbers, dono ke pahade mein aane wala number dhoondo. Dono ko us par badal kar upar ke numbers jodo.
simpler.en: Find a number in the times tables of both bottom numbers of 2/5 and 1/3. Change both to it and add the tops.

prompt.hi: Ek bottle mein 7/8 litre doodh tha. Chai mein 1/2 litre doodh lag gaya. Bottle mein kitna doodh bacha?
prompt.en: A bottle had 7/8 litre of milk. 1/2 litre of milk went into the tea. How much milk is left in the bottle?

simpler.hi: 1/2 ko aathve hisson mein badlo. Phir use 7/8 mein se ghatao.
simpler.en: Change 1/2 into eighths. Then take it away from 7/8.

prompt.hi: {friend} ne sawaal 1/3 + 1/4 ka jawab 2/7 likha. Sahi jawab kitna hai?
prompt.en: {friend} wrote 2/7 as the answer to the question 1/3 + 1/4. What is the correct answer?

why.hi: sawaal 1/3 + 1/4 mein 1/3 = 4/12 aur 1/4 = 3/12, toh 7/12; likha 2/7 galat hai
why.en: in the question 1/3 + 1/4, 1/3 = 4/12 and 1/4 = 3/12, so 7/12; the 2/7 written is wrong

simpler.hi: Neeche wale numbers ko jod dena hi galti hai. Pehle dono bhinnon ko ek common neeche wale number par badlo.
simpler.en: Adding the bottom numbers is the mistake. First change both fractions to one common bottom number.

ladder.why: same idea on a fraction strip in eighths: 1/4 covers 2 eighths
compare two sums with a shared third: 1/3 + 1/3 against 1/3 + 1/6, and by how much
taking away with twelfths: 2/3 − 1/4, both fractions renamed
unlike take-away in a recipe: how much more oats to add

remediation.move: sense first, on a line with halves above and fifths below: 2/5 sits before 1/2, but 1/2 litre plus 1/3 litre must be more than 1/2 litre → adding the bottoms cannot be right → change to same-size parts first

say.hi: Upar se upar aur neeche se neeche jodo, toh jawab dono bhinnon mein bade wale se zyada nahi hota. Par kuch aur jodne par kul badhna chahiye. Isliye pehle dono ko ek size ke hisson mein badlo, phir upar ke number jodo.
say.en: Add top to top and bottom to bottom, and the answer is never more than the bigger fraction. But adding more must make the total grow. So first change both into same-size parts, then add the tops.

simpler.hi: Neeche wale number jodne se jawab chhota reh jaata hai. Pehle ek size ke hisse banao.
simpler.en: Adding the bottom numbers leaves the answer too small. First make same-size parts.

prompt.hi: Ravi ne somvaar ko kitaab ka 1/5 hissa padha, mangalvaar ko 1/2. Do din mein kitaab ka kitna hissa padha?
prompt.en: Ravi read 1/5 of a book on Monday and 1/2 of it on Tuesday. How much of the book did he read in the two days?

simpler.hi: 1/5 aur 1/2 dono ko dasve hisson mein badlo. Phir upar ke numbers jodo.
simpler.en: Change both 1/5 and 1/2 into tenths. Then add the top numbers.

remediation.move: a half laid over a line in sixths: the half covers 3 sixths, not 1 → 1/2 = 3/6; the bottom × 3 means the top × 3 too

say.hi: Neeche ko jis number se guna kiya, upar ko bhi usi se guna karna padta hai. Sirf neeche ka number badhaya, toh har hissa chhota ho gaya par hisson ki ginti utni hi rahi, aur bhinn ki value ghat gayi.
say.en: Whatever the bottom is multiplied by, the top must be multiplied by too. If only the bottom grows, each part gets smaller but the count of parts stays the same, and the fraction's value drops.

simpler.hi: Upar aur neeche dono ko ek hi number se guna karo.
simpler.en: Multiply the top and the bottom by the same number.

prompt.hi: 1/3 aur 1/9 jodo. Pehle 1/3 ko naven hisson mein badlo. Jod kitna hai?
prompt.en: Add 1/3 and 1/9. First change 1/3 into ninths. What is the sum?

simpler.hi: 1/3 ke upar aur neeche dono ko teen se guna karo. Phir usmein 1/9 jodo.
simpler.en: Multiply both the top and bottom of 1/3 by three. Then add 1/9 to it.

bridgeToNext.hi: Ab tak sirf 1 se chhote bhinn the. Agle hisse mein mishrit bhinn jodenge aur ghatayenge, jinmein poore bhi hote hain aur ek hissa bhi.
bridgeToNext.en: So far the fractions were all less than 1. In the next part we will add and subtract mixed fractions, which have wholes and a part too.

simpler.hi: Ab mishrit bhinn jodenge, jinmein poore bhi hote hain aur hissa bhi. Board par poore aur hisse alag-alag rakhe hain.
simpler.en: Now we add mixed fractions, which have wholes and a part too. On the board the wholes and the parts are kept separate.

hook.convey: mixed fraction = wholes + a part → wholes with wholes, parts with parts (same-size parts first); a part sum past 1 gives one more whole; a part too small to take from borrows one whole; a mountain trek in km, a recipe in cups

use.hi: Pahad ki trekking mein pehle din 2 1/2 km aur doosre din 1 3/4 km chalna hai. Kul doori mein poore km aur km ke hisse, dono alag-alag judte hain.
use.en: On a mountain trek you walk 2 1/2 km on the first day and 1 3/4 km on the second. In the total distance, the whole km and the parts of a km are added separately.

use.hi: Halwa ki recipe mein 1 1/2 cup sooji aur 3/4 cup cheeni lagti hai. Rasoi mein aise mishrit bhinn roz jode aur ghataye jaate hain.
use.en: A halwa recipe takes 1 1/2 cups of semolina and 3/4 cup of sugar. In the kitchen, mixed fractions like these are added and taken away every day.

explain.convey: 2 1/5 + 1 2/5: wholes 2 + 1 = 3, parts 1/5 + 2/5 = 3/5 → 3 3/5; the child adds 3 1/6 + 2 4/6 the same way

point.hi: Mishrit bhinn mein poore bhi hote hain aur ek hissa bhi. 2 1/5 + 1 2/5 mein pehle poore jodo: 2 aur 1 se 3 poore. Phir hisse jodo: 1/5 + 2/5 = 3/5. Dono milakar jawab 3 3/5.
point.en: A mixed fraction has wholes and a part too. In 2 1/5 + 1 2/5, first add the wholes: 2 and 1 make 3 wholes. Then add the parts: 1/5 + 2/5 = 3/5. Together the answer is 3 3/5.

prompt.hi: Isi tarah 3 1/6 aur 2 4/6 ko jodo. Jod kitna hai?
prompt.en: In the same way, add 3 1/6 and 2 4/6. What is the sum?

why.hi: poore 3 + 2 = 5 aur hisse 1/6 + 4/6 = 5/6, toh 5 5/6
why.en: wholes 3 + 2 = 5 and parts 1/6 + 4/6 = 5/6, so 5 5/6

simpler.hi: Pehle poore jodo: 2 aur 1 se 3 poore. Phir hisse jodo: 1/5 + 2/5 = 3/5, aur dono ko saath likho.
simpler.en: First add the wholes: 2 and 1 make 3 wholes. Then add the parts: 1/5 + 2/5 = 3/5, and write them together.

explain.convey: parts that add past 1: 1 3/4 + 2 2/4 → wholes make three, parts 3/4 + 2/4 = 5/4; on the line 4/4 is one whole and 5/4 is one gap past it → 5/4 = 1 1/4 → that new whole joins the wholes → 4 1/4; the child does 1 3/4 + 1 3/4

point.hi: 1 3/4 + 2 2/4 mein poore jodo toh teen poore hue. Hisse jodo toh 3/4 + 2/4 = 5/4. Line par dekho: 4/4 par ek poora ho jaata hai, aur 5/4 uske baad ek gap aage hai. Yaani 5/4 = 1 1/4, ek naya poora aur 1/4. Yeh naya poora baaki poore mein jodo, toh jawab 4 1/4.
point.en: In 1 3/4 + 2 2/4, adding the wholes gives three wholes. Adding the parts gives 3/4 + 2/4 = 5/4. Look at the line: at 4/4 one whole is complete, and 5/4 is one gap past it. So 5/4 = 1 1/4, a new whole and 1/4. Add this new whole to the other wholes, and the answer is 4 1/4.

prompt.hi: Ab 1 3/4 aur 1 3/4 ko jodo. Jod kitna hai?
prompt.en: Now add 1 3/4 and 1 3/4. What is the sum?

simpler.hi: Hisse jodkar 5/4 mila, jo 4/4 se ek gap aage hai. Toh 5/4 = 1 1/4, aur yeh naya poora baaki poore mein jod do.
simpler.en: Adding the parts gave 5/4, one gap past 4/4. So 5/4 = 1 1/4, and this new whole joins the other wholes.

explain.convey: taking away when the part on top is too small: 3 1/5 − 1 3/5 → 3/5 cannot come out of 1/5 → open one whole into 5/5: 3 1/5 = 2 6/5 → wholes 2 − 1 = 1, parts 6/5 − 3/5 = 3/5 → 1 3/5; the child does 6 2/7 − 1 5/7 (not 5 3/7)

point.hi: 3 1/5 − 1 3/5 mein 1/5 mein se 3/5 nahi nikal sakta. Isliye 3 poore mein se ek poora kholo, woh 5/5 ban jaata hai: 3 1/5 = 2 6/5. Ab 2 6/5 mein se 1 3/5 nikalo: poore 2 − 1 = 1, aur hisse 6/5 − 3/5 = 3/5. Toh jawab 1 3/5.
point.en: In 3 1/5 − 1 3/5, 3/5 cannot come out of 1/5. So open one of the 3 wholes; it becomes 5/5: 3 1/5 = 2 6/5. Now take 1 3/5 out of 2 6/5: the wholes 2 − 1 = 1, and the parts 6/5 − 3/5 = 3/5. So the answer is 1 3/5.

prompt.hi: Isi tarah 6 2/7 − 1 5/7 kitna hai?
prompt.en: In the same way, what is 6 2/7 − 1 5/7?

why.hi: jaise 3 1/5 = 2 6/5, waise 6 2/7 = 5 9/7; ab 1 5/7 nikalo, toh 4 4/7
why.en: just as 3 1/5 = 2 6/5, 6 2/7 = 5 9/7; take out 1 5/7, and 4 4/7 is left

simpler.hi: 1/5 mein se 3/5 nahi nikal sakta, isliye 3 poore mein se ek khol do, woh 5/5 ban jaata hai. Ab 3 1/5 = 2 6/5, phir ghatao.
simpler.en: 3/5 cannot come out of 1/5, so open one of the 3 wholes into 5/5. Now 3 1/5 = 2 6/5, and then subtract.

problem.hi: Sunita ghar se school tak 1 2/3 km paidal gayi, phir school se market tak 2 1/2 km. Usne kul kitni doori tay ki?
problem.en: Sunita walked 1 2/3 km from home to school, then 2 1/2 km from school to the market. How far did she go in all?

simpler.hi: Pehle poore jodo: 1 aur 2. Phir hisse jodo, 2/3 aur 1/2, unhe ek jaise hisson mein badal kar.
simpler.en: First add the wholes: 1 and 2. Then add the parts, 2/3 and 1/2, after making them the same kind of part.

find.hi: kul doori kitni hai, yaani 1 2/3 + 2 1/2 ka jod

why.hi: poore aur hisse alag-alag jode ja sakte hain
why.en: the wholes and the parts can be added separately

simpler.hi: Poore km aur hisse alag-alag jud sakte hain. Pehle poore jodo: 1 + 2 = 3.
simpler.en: Whole km and parts can be added separately. First add the wholes: 1 + 2 = 3.

do.hi: Hisson ko chhathe hisson mein badlo

why.hi: 3 aur 2 dono ki table mein 6 aata hai, toh dono ek size ke hisse ban jaate hain
why.en: 6 comes in the tables of both 3 and 2, so both become same-size parts

simpler.hi: Tihaai aur aadha alag size ke hisse hain, isliye dono ko chhathe hisson mein badlo. Toh 2/3 = 4/6 aur 1/2 = 3/6.
simpler.en: Thirds and halves are different-size parts, so change both into sixths. Then 2/3 = 4/6 and 1/2 = 3/6.

why.hi: 6/6 se ek poora km banta hai aur 1/6 bachta hai
why.en: 6/6 makes one whole km and 1/6 is left over

simpler.hi: 4/6 + 3/6 = 7/6. Ismein chhah chhathe hisse ek poora km banate hain aur 1/6 bachta hai, toh 1 1/6.
simpler.en: 4/6 + 3/6 = 7/6. Six sixths make one whole km and 1/6 is left, so 1 1/6.

prompt.hi: Ab 3 poore km mein 1 1/6 km jodo. Kul doori kitni hui?
prompt.en: Now add 1 1/6 km to the 3 whole km. What is the total distance?

simpler.hi: 1 1/6 km ka poora 1 km, 3 poore km mein jod do. Phir 1/6 saath likh do.
simpler.en: Add the whole 1 km of 1 1/6 km to the 3 whole km. Then write the 1/6 alongside.

why.hi: poore 1 + 2 = 3, hisse 4/6 + 3/6 = 7/6 = 1 1/6, toh kul 4 1/6 km
why.en: 3 whole km and 7/6 = 1 1/6 km make 4 1/6 km

answer.hi: Sunita ne kul 4 1/6 km doori tay ki

why.hi: poore alag, hisse chhathe mein badal kar jode; 7/6 ka ek poora km poore mein juda; jawab 3 aur 5 ke beech
why.en: wholes added separately, parts changed into sixths and added, the whole km from 7/6 joined them; it lies between 3 and 5

prompt.hi: Ek bori mein 4 1/3 kg chawal tha. Usme se 1 2/3 kg chawal pakaya gaya. Bori mein kitna chawal bacha?
prompt.en: A sack had 4 1/3 kg of rice. 1 2/3 kg of the rice was cooked. How much rice is left in the sack?

simpler.hi: 1/3 mein se 2/3 nahi nikal sakta. Isliye 4 poore mein se ek poora khol kar tihaai hisson mein badlo, phir ghatao.
simpler.en: 2/3 cannot come out of 1/3. So open one of the 4 wholes into thirds, then subtract.

prompt.hi: Mohan ne pehle din 1 3/4 km aur doosre din 2 2/3 km cycle chalayi. Dono din milakar kitni doori hui?
prompt.en: Mohan cycled 1 3/4 km on the first day and 2 2/3 km on the second day. What is the distance for both days together?

why.hi: pehle din 1 3/4, doosre din 2 2/3: poore 3, hisse 9/12 + 8/12 = 1 5/12, kul 4 5/12

simpler.hi: Pehle poore km jodo. Phir 3/4 aur 2/3 ko ek common neeche wale number par badal kar jodo.
simpler.en: First add the whole km. Then change 3/4 and 2/3 to one common bottom number and add them.

prompt.hi: Ek pipe 5 m lamba hai. Usme se 2 3/8 m ka tukda alag kiya gaya. Kitna pipe bacha?
prompt.en: A pipe is 5 m long. A piece 2 3/8 m long was taken off it. How much pipe is left?

why.en: 5 = 4 8/8, so wholes 4 − 2 = 2 and parts 8/8 − 3/8 = 5/8

simpler.hi: 5 m mein se ek poora metre khol kar aathve hisson mein badlo. Uske baad poore se poore aur hisse se hisse ghatao.
simpler.en: Open one whole metre of the 5 m into eighths. After that, take wholes from wholes and parts from parts.

ladder.why: mixed sum with unlike parts: two ropes, 2 1/3 m + 1 1/2 m, thirds and halves into sixths → 3 5/6 m
mixed take-away where the part on top is too small: ribbon for a rakhi stall
mixed take-away with unlike parts and a borrowed whole: cloth for team flags

remediation.move: ribbons: 2 whole ribbons and a quarter; 3 quarters cannot come from 1 quarter → open one whole ribbon into 4 quarters → 2 1/4 = 1 5/4 → now 3/4 comes out of 5/4

say.hi: Jab upar wala hissa nikaalne wale hisse se chhota ho, toh pehle ek poore ko usi size ke hisson mein kholo. Phir poore alag aur hisse alag ghatao.
say.en: When the part you have is smaller than the part to take away, first open one whole into same-size parts. Then subtract the wholes and the parts separately.

simpler.hi: Hissa chhota ho, toh ek poora kholo. Phir ghatao.
simpler.en: If the part is too small, open one whole. Then subtract.

prompt.hi: Ek rassi 4 1/6 m lambi thi. Usme se 1 5/6 m istemaal hui. Kitni rassi bachi?
prompt.en: A rope was 4 1/6 m long. 1 5/6 m of it was used. How much rope is left?

simpler.hi: 1/6 mein se 5/6 nahi nikal sakta. Isliye 4 poore mein se ek khol kar chhathe hisson mein badlo, phir ghatao.
simpler.en: 5/6 cannot come out of 1/6. So open one of the 4 wholes into sixths, then subtract.

remediation.move: mixed fractions keep the same rule: wholes with wholes; parts into same-size parts first (halves and thirds into sixths), never bottom + bottom

say.hi: Mishrit bhinn mein bhi neeche ke number nahi jodte. Poore alag jodo, aur hisson ko pehle ek size ke hisson mein badlo, phir jodo.
say.en: In mixed fractions too, the bottom numbers are never added. Add the wholes separately, and first change the parts into same-size parts, then add them.

simpler.hi: Poore alag jodo. Hisse pehle ek size ke banao, phir jodo.
simpler.en: Add the wholes on their own. Make the parts one size first, then add.

prompt.hi: Pehli bottle mein 1 1/4 litre aur doosri bottle mein 2 1/2 litre paani hai. Kul kitna paani hai?
prompt.en: The first bottle has 1 1/4 litres of water and the second bottle 2 1/2 litres. How much water is there in all?

why.hi: pehli bottle 1 1/4, doosri bottle 2 1/2 = 2 2/4: poore 3, hisse 3/4, kul 3 3/4
why.en: wholes 1 + 2 = 3, and 1/2 = 2/4 so parts 1/4 + 2/4 = 3/4

simpler.hi: Pehle poore litre jodo. Phir 1/2 ko chauthai hisson mein badal kar 1/4 mein jodo.
simpler.en: First add the whole litres. Then change 1/2 into quarters and add it to 1/4.
